compute.cost_note: stdlib only (n-gram counting and curated templates); no spaCy, no API costs

do_not_use_when: you have no baseline; lexical-bundle and hapax-survival categories need --baseline-dir
you want an authorship verdict; survival rates are descriptive

examples.description: Phrase-frame survival against a personal baseline

optional: optional flags --baseline-dir (needed for lexical_bundles and hapax_phrase_survival), --category, --keep-quotes, --bundle-min-count, --hapax-n, --json, --out (see --help)
inputs.target: one .txt/.md target plus a baseline directory of the writer's prose

purpose: Phrase-frame mining over the writer's reusable language frames. Reports lexical bundles, slot frames ("not just X but Y"), curated idioms, hapax-phrase survival and stance/intensifier frames: per-frame counts, baseline-frame survival rate in the target, and density per 1,000 target words. The frame-level complement to idiolect_detector's word-level keyness.
use_when: checking whether a revised draft kept the writer's recurring phrase frames
pairing with idiolect_detector for a phrase-level voice-preservation read
